note.note:
History:
- Chief complaint: Sudden inability to move the left arm upon waking this morning (~1 hour prior to call).
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began on waking today; persistent at time of call.
- Progression: Ongoing; patient reports speech is getting “a bit harder.”
- Associated symptoms: Left facial tingling since onset; difficulty swallowing; difficulty speaking (slower, more effortful). Spilled drink earlier. No left leg symptoms. No hand discoloration; arm/hand not cold. No pain.
- Triggers/context: Slept as usual; no awkward position or different bed. First episode.
- Social: Lives alone. Former smoker. Alcohol: beers (pints) — a few on weekends and a couple during the week.
- Family history: Father with heart disease.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Hypertension.
- Allergies: Penicillin.
- Medications:
  - Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Losartan — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Amlodipine — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Mode: Telephone consult; no visual/in-person examination performed.
- Reported findings:
  - Unable to move left arm; no pain.
  - Left facial tingling.
  - Dysphagia (difficulty swallowing).
  - Subjective speech difficulty (slower, requires more effort).
  - No facial asymmetry noticed by patient.
  - No discoloration or coldness of the left hand.
  - No left leg symptoms reported.

Impression:
- Suspected acute cerebrovascular event (stroke) given sudden left arm paralysis with facial paresthesia, dysphagia, and speech difficulty.

Management Plan:
- Emergency response initiated: Ambulance arranged to patient’s home for immediate transfer to ED/A&E for stroke assessment.
- Safety instructions: Unlock front door and sit in the hallway to allow access.
- Clinician remained on the line until ambulance arrival.
- Anticipated hospital course communicated: ED to involve stroke team to assess for potential acute stroke treatment.

Patient Summary:
- Patient awoke with sudden left arm paralysis, left facial tingling, dysphagia, and speech difficulty. Clinical picture concerning for acute stroke. Ambulance dispatched for urgent hospital evaluation and management.

Key Takeaways:
- This is an emergency; patient is being transported by ambulance for stroke evaluation.
- Keep the front door unlocked and stay seated near the entrance until help arrives.

Next Steps:
- Hospital stroke team assessment and urgent management per stroke protocol.
- Further investigations and treatment to be determined by the ED/stroke team.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing expected elements: Vital signs; exact time last known well; detailed neurologic exam (NIHSS/FAST findings); medication doses and schedules; antiplatelet/anticoagulant use; blood glucose; details of penicillin reaction; imaging/lab results.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Telephone-only; some pauses/partial words; no visual exam possible.
